- Conversely, if we over-provision Reserved capacity and need to downscale after the pilot, what credits or downgrade options exist?

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can support a hybrid pattern and we have documented upgrade/downgrade paths that are designed for pilots. High-level options below; I attached a short pricing spreadsheet and an SOW template for your review.

Option A — Cost-first (Compact -> Elastic as needed)
- Start Compact (hosted): lowest unit cost but limited sustained throughput.
- If traffic spikes, auto-fallback to Elastic (hosted) or Dedicated variant per routing policy.
- Upgrade is immediate (no model re-commit), token accounting pro-rates the host usage vs. new capacity for billing in the same billing period.
- Downgrade: we allow step-down within the month; Reserved credits are applied per the reserved contract (see below).

Option B — Hybrid (Dedicated for batch + hosted for day)
- Dedicated pool reserved for nightly batch (guaranteed throughput).
- Daytime interactive uses hosted API; requests routed by policy to keep latency low.
- This avoids overcommitting dedicated GPUs for daytime spikes and keeps predictability for heavy batch jobs.

Add-ons and features
- Extended KV cache and quantization profiles are available as add-ons or bundled into our Elastic+ and Dedicated+ tiers.
- We can enable quantization profiles on request (subject to model compatibility).

Pricing and credits
- Attached: BrightMed_pricing_v2.xlsx with two example scenarios (monthly and annual commit).
- For pilots, we typically offer a one-time migration credit (applied to the first invoice) and provide a 30% first-quarter usage credit for new reserved commits to offset trial variance.

Next steps
- I'll send a mutual action plan doc after you confirm the pilot dates. Can you do a call tomorrow at 10am PT or Wednesday 1pm PT?

Thanks — copying Karthik for technical sizing and Priyom for commercial terms.

Cheers,
Mina Haddad

Internal — notes and recommended language to send to customer. Do not forward verbatim.

Recommended offer (pilot-friendly):
- 8–12 week pilot: provide a one-time $7k migration credit + 30% usage credit on first 60 days of any new Reserved commit. Credits apply to invoice line items for tokens and embeddings.
- Downgrade path: allow step-down after 30 days with formal 30-day notice. Reserved capacity that is unused can be converted into platform credits valid for 6 months; refunds only for annual prepayments in exceptional cases and require revenue approval.
- Quantization/extended KV cache: charge a one-time enablement fee ($1,500) for engineering validation + a small recurring premium (5–8%) for the feature retention and monitoring.

Operationally: propose a canary migration plan — route 10% of traffic to Dedicated for two nights, evaluate tail latency and cost, then ramp. For billing conversation, Priyom should propose a 10% early-commit discount on year-one ARR if they commit to >= 6 months of reserved for batch.
